svg.title: Simplified mock-up of the Register New Step dialog
svg.desc: A simplified drawing of the Register New Step dialog in the Plug-in Registration Tool, filled in for Cedar step R1. Left column: Message Update, Primary Entity cedar_workorder, Secondary Entity empty, Filtering Attributes cedar_fieldlinkstatus, Event Handler Cedar.Service.Plugins.WorkOrderRejectedPlugin, Step Name Cedar: WO rejected – Update – PostOperation async, Run in User's Context Cedar Automation, Execution Order 10. Lower left: Event Pipeline Stage of Execution PostOperation, Execution Mode Asynchronous, Deployment Server, and the check box Delete AsyncOperation if StatusCode = Successful ticked. Right column: Unsecure Configuration text box and Secure Configuration text box. Numbered notes explain each group.
svg.text: Register New Step (simplified drawing) filled in for Cedar step R1
(empty for R1; G1 and G2 hold
1 Message + Primary Entity decide which operations can start the step. Always set the table when the message has one.
2 Update only: the step runs when one of these columns is in the request, changed or not. Never tick the primary key.
3 Calling User by default. Another user changes context.UserId for the whole step; InitiatingUserId stays the real caller.
4 Lowest number first within a stage. Equal numbers run in no guaranteed order: set it deliberately (Cedar: 10, 20, 30).
5 Asynchronous is offered only with PostOperation. The step becomes a system job after the commit.
6 Removes the system job row when it succeeds, which keeps the AsyncOperation table small. Failed jobs stay for diagnosis.
7 Two strings handed to the class constructor. Unsecure travels in the solution; secure does not and only administrators can read it.
